# Script
```{r}
# Load  delta travel time and population distribution
## For delta travel time go to script 05. maps_tt_and_delta_TT
### After doing so make a list using the following code:

delta_tt_list <- mget(ls(pattern = "delta_tt_all"))

## Load population distribution
pop_density_raster <- rast("C:/Users/rikib/Onedrive/PhD_Undernutrition_Uganda_Physical_Accessbility/2_Study_2_Flooding_Analysis/InAccessmod/Uganda/data/rPopulation/20240308161107/processed/UG_total_10m.tif")

# Load the SpatVector for parish boundaries
parish_boundaries = vect("C:/Users/rikib/Onedrive/PhD_Undernutrition_Uganda_Physical_Accessbility/2_Study_2_Flooding_Analysis/Data/Processed/Adm_boundaries_parishes/Parishes_Kamp_UTM36N.shp")

# Align the population density raster and the delta travel time rasters 
parish_boundaries <- Spatial.align::align(parish_boundaries, pop_density_raster, show_plot = FALSE)

# Align the delta travel time rasters to the parish boundaries
delta_tt_list <- lapply(delta_tt_list, function(delta_tt_raster) {
  delta_tt_raster <- Spatial.align::align(delta_tt_raster, pop_density_raster, show_plot = FALSE)
  return(delta_tt_raster)
})


# Step 1: Iterate through each delta_tt_raster in delta_tt_list and multiply by population density raster
weighted_delta_tt_list <- lapply(delta_tt_list, function(delta_tt_raster) {
  # Multiply each delta_tt_raster by the population density raster
  weighted_delta_tt_raster <- delta_tt_raster * pop_density_raster
  return(weighted_delta_tt_raster)
})

# Assign new names to the weighted_delta_tt_list
names(weighted_delta_tt_list) <- sapply(names(weighted_delta_tt_list), function(name) {
    parts <- strsplit(name, "_")[[1]]
    paste(tail(parts, 2), collapse = "_")
})

# Step 2: Perform zonal statistics to sum the weighted delta travel time for each parish and save to parish_boundaries object
# Loop through each weighted delta travel time raster and perform zonal statistics
for (i in seq_along(weighted_delta_tt_list)) {
    # Perform zonal statistics to sum the weighted delta travel time for each parish
    sum_weighted_delta_tt <- zonal(weighted_delta_tt_list[[i]], parish_boundaries, fun = "sum", na.rm = TRUE)
    # Save the result to the parish_boundaries object using the original name
    original_name <- names(weighted_delta_tt_list)[i]
    parish_boundaries[[paste0("Weighted_delta_tt_", original_name)]] <- sum_weighted_delta_tt[, 1]
}

# Step 3: Sum population density across all cells in each parish and save it in the parish_boundaries object
parish_boundaries$Population_Sum <- zonal(pop_density_raster, parish_boundaries, fun = "sum", na.rm = TRUE)

# Step 4: Calculate the impacted weighted delta travel time for each parish
# Loop through each scenario and calculate the impacted weighted delta travel time for each parish
for (i in seq_along(weighted_delta_tt_list)) {
    # Calculate the impacted weighted delta travel time for each parish
    original_name <- names(weighted_delta_tt_list)[i]
    parish_boundaries[[paste0("Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_", original_name)]] <- parish_boundaries[[paste0("Weighted_delta_tt_", original_name)]] / parish_boundaries$Population_Sum
}

# Step 5: Plot 
# List of column names that will be used for the fill
scenario_columns <- grep("Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_", names(parish_boundaries), value = TRUE)

# Create an empty list to store the plots
plot_list <- list()

# Determine the global range for the impacted weighted delta travel time
global_range <- range(unlist(lapply(scenario_columns, function(col) parish_boundaries[[col]])), na.rm = TRUE)

# Reorder scenario_columns to start with 20, 40, 60, 80, 100 and also by 1, 3, 6 hours
scenario_columns_ordered <- scenario_columns[order(
  as.numeric(sub(".*_(\\d+)_.*", "\\1", scenario_columns)),   # Sort by mm
  as.numeric(sub(".*_(\\d+)$", "\\1", sub(".*_\\d+_", "", scenario_columns)))  # Sort by seconds (3600, 10800, etc.)
)]
# Loop through the reordered scenario columns and create the plots
for (i in seq_along(scenario_columns_ordered)) {
    # Extract the two numbers from the scenario column name
    numbers <- sub(".*_(\\d+)_(\\d+)$", "\\1 \\2", scenario_columns_ordered[i])
    numbers_split <- unlist(strsplit(numbers, " "))
    
    # Convert the second number from seconds to hours (3600 seconds = 1 hour)
    hours <- as.numeric(numbers_split[2]) / 3600
    
    # Create the formatted title: "X mm x Y hours"
    title_part <- paste(numbers_split[1], "mm x", hours, "hour")
    
    # Dynamically create the plot for each fill
    p <- ggplot() +
        geom_spatvector(data = parish_boundaries, aes(fill = .data[[scenario_columns_ordered[i]]])) +  # Dynamic fill
        scale_fill_viridis_c(
            option = "magma",  # Use the magma color palette
            name = "Delta Travel\nTime Decrease",  # Legend title
            na.value = "transparent",  # Hide NAs by making them transparent
            limits = global_range  # Standardize the scale
        ) +
        theme_minimal() +
        ggtitle(paste("Scenario", title_part)) +  # Use the formatted title
        theme(
            legend.position = "bottom",  # Move the legend to the bottom
            legend.title = element_text(size = 12),  # Increase legend title font size
            legend.text = element_text(size = 10),  # Increase legend label font size
            axis.text = element_blank(),  # Remove axis text
            axis.title = element_blank(),  # Remove axis titles
            panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray80", size = 0.5),  # Add major gridlines
            panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "gray90", size = 0.25),  # Add minor gridlines
            strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white")  # Add white background to facet labels
        )

    # Store the plot in the list
    plot_list[[i]] <- p
}

# Combine the plots in a grid layout using patchwork and add a shared legend
final_plot <- wrap_plots(plot_list, ncol = 3) + 
    plot_layout(guides = "collect") & 
    theme(legend.position = "right") & 
    plot_annotation(
        title = "Average Population Weighted Delta Travel Time Scenarios per Parish",
        theme = theme(
            plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold")
        )
    )

# Display the combined plot
print(final_plot)

# Filter the specific scenarios for 20mm x 6hr and 100mm x 1hr
specific_scenarios <- c("Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_20_21600", "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_100_3600")

# Create an empty list to store the specific scenario plots
specific_plot_list <- list()

# Loop through the specific scenarios and create the plots
for (i in seq_along(specific_scenarios)) {
    # Extract the column name for the current scenario
    scenario_col <- specific_scenarios[i]
    
    # Extract the two numbers from the scenario column name
    numbers <- sub(".*_(\\d+)_(\\d+)$", "\\1 \\2", scenario_col)
    numbers_split <- unlist(strsplit(numbers, " "))
    
    # Convert the second number from seconds to hours (3600 seconds = 1 hour)
    hours <- as.numeric(numbers_split[2]) / 3600
    
    # Create the formatted title: "X mm x Y hours"
    title_part <- paste(numbers_split[1], "mm x", hours, "hour")
    
    # Dynamically create the plot for each fill
    p <- ggplot() +
        geom_spatvector(data = parish_boundaries, aes(fill = .data[[scenario_col]])) +  # Dynamic fill
        scale_fill_viridis_c(
            option = "magma",  # Use the magma color palette
            name = "Delta Travel\nTime Decrease",  # Legend title
            na.value = "transparent",  # Hide NAs by making them transparent
            limits = global_range  # Standardize the scale
        ) +
        theme_minimal() +
        ggtitle(paste("Scenario", title_part)) +  # Use the formatted title
        theme(
            legend.position = "bottom",  # Move the legend to the bottom
            legend.title = element_text(size = 12),  # Increase legend title font size
            legend.text = element_text(size = 10),  # Increase legend label font size
            axis.text = element_blank(),  # Remove axis text
            axis.title = element_blank(),  # Remove axis titles
            panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray80", size = 0.5),  # Add major gridlines
            panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "gray90", size = 0.25),  # Add minor gridlines
            strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white")  # Add white background to facet labels
        )

    # Store the plot in the list
    specific_plot_list[[i]] <- p
}

# Combine the specific scenario plots in a grid layout using patchwork
specific_final_plot <- wrap_plots(specific_plot_list, ncol = 2) + 
    plot_layout(guides = "collect") & 
    theme(legend.position = "right") & 
    plot_annotation(
        title = "Average Population Weighted Delta Travel Time for Specific Scenarios per Parish",
        theme = theme(
            plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold")
        )
    )

# Display the combined specific scenario plot
print(specific_final_plot)

```

# Highlight parishes with the highest decrease in travel time for each scenario
```{r}	
# Function to format scenario titles (e.g., "100_21600" -> "100 mm x 6 hours")
format_scenario_title <- function(scenario) {
    # Extract the two numbers from the scenario name
    numbers <- sub(".*_(\\d+)_(\\d+)$", "\\1 \\2", scenario)
    numbers_split <- unlist(strsplit(numbers, " "))
    
    # Convert the second number from seconds to hours (3600 seconds = 1 hour)
    hours <- as.numeric(numbers_split[2]) / 3600
    
    # Format the title as "X mm x Y hours"
    formatted_title <- paste(numbers_split[1], "mm x", hours, "hours")
    
    return(formatted_title)
}

# Define the list of columns for the 15 Average Weighted Delta TT scenarios
scenario_columns_ordered <- c(
    "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_20_3600", "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_20_10800", "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_20_21600",
    "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_40_3600", "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_40_10800", "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_40_21600",
    "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_60_3600", "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_60_10800", "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_60_21600",
    "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_80_3600", "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_80_10800", "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_80_21600",
    "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_100_3600", "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_100_10800", "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_100_21600"
)

# Convert the SpatVector object to a data frame
parish_boundaries_df <- as.data.frame(parish_boundaries)

# Create an empty list to store the top parishes for each scenario
top_parishes_list <- list()

for (i in seq_along(scenario_columns_ordered)) {
    # Extract the column name for the current scenario
    scenario_col <- scenario_columns_ordered[i]
    
    # Check if the column exists in the data frame
    if (scenario_col %in% names(parish_boundaries_df)) {
        # Access the travel time values in the current scenario column
        travel_times <- parish_boundaries_df[[scenario_col]]
        
        # Check if 'travel_times' is numeric and proceed
        if (!any(is.na(travel_times))) {
            # Find the top 10 parishes with the lowest travel time decrease for the current scenario
            top_parishes <- parish_boundaries_df[order(travel_times), ][1:10, ]  # Sort in ascending order
            
            # Store the top parishes in the list, including the parish names and travel time
            top_parishes_list[[scenario_col]] <- data.frame(
                Parish_Name = top_parishes$PName2016,
                Travel_Time_Decrease = top_parishes[[scenario_col]],  # Use the values from the scenario column
                Scenario = scenario_col
            )
        } else {
            warning(paste("Scenario column", scenario_col, "contains non-numeric data. Skipping."))
        }
    } else {
        warning(paste("Scenario column", scenario_col, "not found in data. Skipping."))
    }
}

# Print the top 10 parishes for each scenario with clearer formatting
for (scenario in names(top_parishes_list)) {
    formatted_title <- format_scenario_title(scenario)
    
    cat("\n\n============================\n")
    cat("Top 10 Parishes for Scenario:", formatted_title, "\n")
    cat("============================\n\n")
    
    # Print the table for the current scenario without the 'Scenario' column
    print(top_parishes_list[[scenario]][, c("Parish_Name", "Travel_Time_Decrease")])
    
    cat("\n")  # Add extra spacing between scenarios
}

# Create an overall table showing the frequency of each parish in the top 10
parish_frequency <- table(unlist(lapply(top_parishes_list, function(df) df$Parish_Name)))

# Convert the table to a data frame
parish_frequency_df <- as.data.frame(parish_frequency)

# Rename the columns appropriately (Var1 is the parish name, Freq is the frequency)
colnames(parish_frequency_df) <- c("Parish_Name", "Frequency")

# Ensure the Frequency column is numeric
parish_frequency_df$Frequency <- as.numeric(parish_frequency_df$Frequency)

# Order the frequency table by Frequency in descending order
parish_frequency_df <- parish_frequency_df[order(-parish_frequency_df$Frequency), ]

# Limit the output to the top 10 parishes
top_10_parish_frequency <- head(parish_frequency_df, 10)

# Print the top 10 parishes based on their frequency
cat("\n\nTop 10 Parishes by Frequency in Top 10 Lists:\n")
print(top_10_parish_frequency)

# Highlight the top 10 parishes on a map 
# Create a new column in the parish boundaries data frame to indicate if a parish is in the top 10
parish_boundaries$Top_10 <- ifelse(parish_boundaries$PName2016 %in% top_10_parish_frequency$Parish_Name, "Top 10", "Not in Top 10")

# Create a color palette for the top 10 parishes
top_10_palette <- c("Top 10" = "red", "Not in Top 10" = "gray")

# Create the plot highlighting the top 10 parishes
highlighted_plot <- ggplot() +
    geom_spatvector(data = parish_boundaries, aes(fill = Top_10)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = top_10_palette, name = "Top 10 Parishes") +
    theme_minimal() +
    ggtitle("Top 10 Parishes with Highest Travel Time Decrease") +
    theme(
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.title = element_text(size = 12),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
        axis.text = element_blank(),
        axis.title = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray80", size = 0.5),
        panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "gray90", size = 0.25),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "white")
    )

# Display the highlighted plot
print(highlighted_plot)
```

# Densitiy plots of the average weighted delta travel time for each scenario across all parishes
```{r}
# Define the list of columns for the 15 Average Weighted Delta TT scenarios
scenario_columns_ordered <- c(
    "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_20_3600", "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_20_10800", "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_20_21600",
    "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_40_3600", "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_40_10800", "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_40_21600",
    "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_60_3600", "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_60_10800", "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_60_21600",
    "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_80_3600", "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_80_10800", "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_80_21600",
    "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_100_3600", "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_100_10800", "Average_Weighted_Delta_TT_100_21600"
)

# Get the global x and y limits based on all scenario columns
# Global x limits based on the range of all scenario columns
x_limits <- range(unlist(parish_boundaries_df[scenario_columns_ordered]))

# You could choose a uniform y-axis limit or calculate it across all scenarios
# Since we are using density plots, y-limits can vary, so we can calculate it
y_limits <- c(0, max(sapply(scenario_columns_ordered, function(col) {
    max(density(parish_boundaries_df[[col]], na.rm = TRUE)$y)
})))

# Create an empty list to store the density plots
density_plot_list <- list()

# Loop through each scenario column and create the density plots
for (i in seq_along(scenario_columns_ordered)) {
    # Extract the column name for the current scenario
    scenario_col <- scenario_columns_ordered[i]
    
    # Check if the column exists in the data frame
    if (scenario_col %in% names(parish_boundaries_df)) {
        # Create the density plot for the current scenario by directly referencing the column
        p <- ggplot(parish_boundaries_df, aes(x = .data[[scenario_col]])) +  # Reference the column dynamically
            geom_density(fill = "blue", color = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
            xlim(x_limits) +  # Set global x limits
            ylim(y_limits) +  # Set global y limits
            theme_minimal() +
            ggtitle(format_scenario_title(scenario_col)) +  # Format the title dynamically
            xlab("Average Weighted Delta Travel Time") +
            ylab("Density") +
            theme(
                plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
                axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
                axis.text = element_text(size = 10)
            )
        
        # Store the density plot in the list
        density_plot_list[[i]] <- p
    }
}

# Combine the density plots in a grid layout using patchwork
final_density_plot <- wrap_plots(density_plot_list, ncol = 3) + 
    plot_layout(guides = "collect") & 
    plot_annotation(
        title = "Density Plots of Average Weighted Delta Travel Time Scenarios per Parish",
        theme = theme(
            plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold")
        )
    )

# Display the combined density plot
print(final_density_plot)

# Overlayed density plots for different mm but same hours (e.g., 20 -100 x 1 hour) 
# Create an empty list to store the overlayed plots
overlayed_plot_list <- list()

# Define the hours and corresponding scenario columns for each group
hours_list <- c(3600, 10800, 21600)  # 1 hour, 3 hours, 6 hours

# Define the color palette for the mm values
color_palette <- c("blue", "green", "orange", "purple", "red")

# Loop through each hour to create overlayed density plots for different mm values
for (hour in hours_list) {
    
    # Filter scenario columns that match the current hour
    scenarios_for_hour <- grep(paste0("_", hour), scenario_columns_ordered, value = TRUE)
    
    # Create an empty data frame to store mm and travel times
    combined_df <- data.frame()
    
    # Collect all travel times and corresponding mm values for the current hour
    for (scenario_col in scenarios_for_hour) {
        # Extract mm from the scenario column
        mm_value <- sub(".*_(\\d+)_\\d+$", "\\1", scenario_col)
        
        # Create a temporary data frame with the mm values and travel times
        temp_df <- data.frame(
            mm = as.numeric(mm_value),  # Ensure mm is numeric for correct ordering
            travel_times = parish_boundaries_df[[scenario_col]]
        )
        
        # Combine this data into the master data frame for this hour
        combined_df <- rbind(combined_df, temp_df)
    }
    
    # Create the overlayed density plot for the current hour
    p <- ggplot(combined_df, aes(x = travel_times, color = as.factor(mm))) +  # Color by mm values
        geom_density(fill = NA, alpha = 0.7) +
        theme_minimal() +
        ggtitle(paste(hour / 3600, "hour(s)")) +
        xlab("Average Weighted Delta Travel Time") +
        ylab("Density") +
        scale_color_manual(values = color_palette, name = "mm Values", breaks = c(20, 40, 60, 80, 100)) +  # Order mm from 20 to 100
        theme(
            plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14, face = "bold"),
            axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
            axis.text = element_text(size = 10)
        )
    
    # Store the overlayed plot in the list
    overlayed_plot_list[[as.character(hour)]] <- p
}

# Combine the overlayed plots in a grid layout using patchwork
final_overlayed_plot <- wrap_plots(overlayed_plot_list, ncol = 1) + 
    plot_annotation(
        title = "Overlayed Density Plots for Different mm by Hours",
        theme = theme(
            plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 16, face = "bold")
        )
    )

# Display the combined overlayed density plots
print(final_overlayed_plot)
```
